# Goal: loc skips what a project ignores

`loc` counts every file under a folder. Projects keep files there they don't want counted:
vendored code, fixtures, generated files. Give `loc` an ignore file, then use it in the scan and
the command. No new dependencies.

1. `ignoreMatcher(root: string): Promise<(path: string, isFolder: boolean) => boolean>`, exported
   from `src/index.ts`. It reads `<root>/.locignore` (when there is none, nothing is ignored) and
   answers whether a path is ignored. `path` is relative to `root`, with `/` separators. The
   file's syntax is a subset of `.gitignore`'s:
   - one pattern a line; blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; trailing spaces
     are trimmed;
   - `*` matches any characters but `/`; `?` matches one character but `/`; `**` matches across
     folders: `**/x` (x at any depth), `x/**` (everything inside x), `a/**/b` (b under a, at any
     depth, `a/b` included);
   - a pattern with no `/`, or only a trailing one, matches a name at any depth (`*.log`,
     `build`); a pattern with a `/` at its start or in its middle is relative to `root` (`/dist`,
     `src/gen`);
   - a trailing `/` matches folders only (`out/`);
   - a path is ignored when it, or one of the folders it is in, matches;
   - `!pattern` includes again what an earlier pattern ignored; the last pattern that matches
     wins. As in git, a file cannot be included again when a folder it is in is ignored.
2. `scanFolder(root, options?)` leaves out what `ignoreMatcher(root)` ignores (files, and folders
   with everything in them) unless `options.ignore` is `false`; the `.locignore` file itself is
   counted like any other file. The command does the same, and takes `--no-ignore` to count
   everything.

facts: src/scan.ts: `scanFolder(root: string): Promise<FileCount[]>` walks with readdir withFileTypes, builds rel paths with `/` (`rel ? `${rel}/${name}` : name`), skips symlinks, `.git`, `node_modules`, binaries; sorts by path.
src/index.ts re-exports countLines, languageOf, types, and scanFolder/summarize/types from './scan.js'; no ignore module exists yet.
src/cli.ts parses argv by hand: `--json` flag; any other arg starting with `-` fails with 'unknown option' exit 2; folder defaults to '.'; calls `summarize(await scanFolder(folder))`.
test/scan.test.ts has a `folder(files)` helper creating a temp dir via mkdtempSync; tests import from '../src/index.js'.
tsconfig: strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, NodeNext; `npm run check` = tsc + vitest run.
README.md lists src modules briefly; does not document the CLI.
No dependencies may be added (CLAUDE.md); matching must be hand-written (no minimatch).
guesses: `.locignore` paths/patterns: reading the file with readFile and treating ENOENT as 'no patterns' is enough; other read errors can propagate.

Pattern compilation to RegExp per pattern (anchored vs any-depth, dirOnly flag, negated flag) is the simplest correct approach; 'ignored when it or a parent folder matches' plus the git re-include rule can be implemented by checking each ancestor prefix (as folder) first: if any ancestor's last-matching rule is an ignore, the path is ignored regardless of later negations.

scanFolder walking can prune ignored folders (call matcher(path, true) before descending) and test files with matcher(path, false); the options type `{ ignore?: boolean }` is new and should be exported as e.g. `ScanOptions`.
The CLI `--no-ignore` flag must be filtered out of `rest` like `--json` so it isn't reported as unknown.
ledger.plan: First build and test `ignoreMatcher` in a new `src/ignore.ts` exported from `src/index.ts`; then, on that branch, make `scanFolder` and the CLI use it with `options.ignore` / `--no-ignore`.

nodes.title: ignoreMatcher: read and match .locignore
nodes.brief: Create `src/ignore.ts` exporting `ignoreMatcher(root: string): Promise<(path: string, isFolder: boolean) => boolean>` and re-export it from `src/index.ts` (`export { ignoreMatcher } from './ignore.js';`). Write the failing tests first in `test/ignore.test.ts` (use a temp dir with a `.locignore`, like the `folder` helper in test/scan.test.ts). Behaviour, exactly per the goal: read `<root>/.locignore`; missing file (ENOENT) → matcher that ignores nothing. One pattern per line; skip blank lines and lines starting with `#`; trim trailing spaces. `*` = any chars except `/`; `?` = one char except `/`; `**/x` = x at any depth; `x/**` = everything inside x; `a/**/b` = b under a at any depth including `a/b`. A pattern with no `/` or only a trailing `/` matches a name at any depth; a leading or middle `/` anchors it to root (`/dist`, `src/gen`). Trailing `/` = folders only. A path is ignored when it or any folder it is in matches. `!pattern` re-includes; last matching pattern wins; but a path cannot be re-included when one of its ancestor folders is ignored (git semantics). `path` is relative to root with `/` separators; `isFolder` says whether it is a folder. Escape regex metacharacters when compiling patterns. No new dependencies; no changes to scan.ts or cli.ts in this workspace. Cover in tests: comments/blank/trailing spaces, `*.log` at depth, `build` matching folder and its contents, `/dist` anchored vs `a/dist` not matched, `src/gen`, `out/` folders-only (file named `out` not ignored), `**/x`, `x/**`, `a/**/b` incl. `a/b`, `?`, negation re-including a file, negation that cannot re-include under an ignored folder, no .locignore. Add a line about `src/ignore.ts` to README.md. `npm run check` must pass.

reviews.summary:
No defects found. I traced the diff by hand and did not run it. The reported `npm run check` passed.

- **Brief behaviour:** `src/ignore.ts` implements everything the brief lists, and the glob rules compile as specified. `a/**/b` compiles to `a/(?:.*/)?b`, so `a/b` matches. `x/**` compiles to `x/.+`, so the folder `x` itself is not matched. `/dist` and `src/gen` are anchored to root, while `build` and `out/` match at any depth.
- **Negation:** `!pattern` and last-match-wins work. A path under an ignored ancestor stays ignored, because ancestors are checked first and return `true`.
- **Missing file:** `ENOENT` returns a matcher that ignores nothing. Other read errors are rethrown.
- **Tests and housekeeping:** `test/ignore.test.ts` covers every case the brief lists. The re-export and the README line are present, and nothing was added to `scan.ts`, `cli.ts` or the dependencies.

nodes.research:
**Findings for `src/ignore.ts`**

**Layout** (flat, small repo): `src/{cli,count,index,languages,scan,types}.ts`, `test/{count,scan}.test.ts`, `README.md`. No `.locignore` handling exists yet.

**Conventions**
- ESM with `NodeNext`: relative imports end in `.js`, and type-only imports use `import type`.
- Code is dense, with terse one-line helpers and few comments. Node imports are written as `node:fs/promises`.
- `src/index.ts` is a list of one-line re-exports. Add `export { ignoreMatcher } from './ignore.js';`.
- `npm run check` runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json && vitest run`. The tests are typechecked too, so `test/ignore.test.ts` must be strict-clean.
- Don't add dependencies. `scan.ts` and `cli.ts` are out of scope for this workspace.

**Test helper to copy** (`test/scan.test.ts:6-13`):
```ts
function folder(files: Record<string,string>): string {
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'loc-'));
  for (const [path,text] of Object.entries(files)) {
    mkdirSync(join(root, path, '..'), {recursive:true});
    writeFileSync(join(root, path), text);
  }
  return root;
}
```
Imports come from `node:fs`, `node:os`, `node:path` and `vitest`. Import the code under test from `../src/index.js`. For the "no .locignore" case, call `folder({})` or `folder({'a.txt':''})`.

**Design notes and traps**
- Read the file with `readFile` from `node:fs/promises`. Catch only `ENOENT` (`(e as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT'`) and rethrow anything else. The matcher then returns `() => false`.
- Split on `\r?\n`. Trim trailing spaces only (`/ +$/`). Skip a line if it is empty or starts with `#`.
- For `!`, strip the prefix and mark the rule as a negation.
- A trailing `/` means folders only. Strip it and set `dirOnly`.
- **Anchoring**: after stripping the trailing `/`, a pattern is anchored if it still contains `/` (leading or middle). Strip the leading `/`. Unanchored patterns match at any depth, so prefix the regex with `(?:^|/)`.
- **Regex compile**, per segment or char:
  - Escape metacharacters, and do `*` → `[^/]*` and `?` → `[^/]`.
  - `**/` at the start → `(?:.*/)?`.
  - `/**/` in the middle → `/(?:.*/)?`, so `a/b` matches.
  - `/**` at the end → `/.+`, meaning everything inside x but not x itself.
  - Handle `**` before the single `*` replacement, with a placeholder or a tokenizer. A char loop is safest.
- **Evaluation** for `(path, isFolder)`:
  1. Walk each ancestor prefix, i.e. `path.split('/')` up to length−1, as folders (`isFolder=true`).
  2. For each ancestor, run the "last matching rule wins" check. If it comes out ignored, return true. This gives the git rule that nothing under an ignored folder can be re-included.
  3. Finally run the same check on the path itself with its own `isFolder`.
  - Each rule match must respect `dirOnly`, which applies only when `isFolder` is true. A file named `out` is therefore not ignored by `out/`.
  - `build` matching "folder and its contents" falls out of the ancestor check.
  - `x/**` matches `x/a`, so the contents are ignored but `x` itself is not.
- Beware the `/dist` vs `a/dist` case. Anchored means the regex is `^dist$`, so `a/dist` is not matched. The unanchored `build` has `(?:^|/)build$`.
- Negation test: `*.log` then `!keep.log` makes `keep.log` included. Separately, `vendor/` then `!vendor/x.js` leaves `vendor/x.js` ignored.

**README**: it has a bullet list (`- \`src/count.ts\`: ...`). Append a line such as ``- `src/ignore.ts`: `ignoreMatcher(root)`, reads `<root>/.locignore` (a subset of `.gitignore`) and says whether a path is ignored.``

nodes.title: scanFolder and the loc command honour .locignore
nodes.brief: Starting from the ignore-matcher branch, which provides `ignoreMatcher(root: string): Promise<(path: string, isFolder: boolean) => boolean>` in `src/ignore.ts`. Change `scanFolder` in `src/scan.ts` to `scanFolder(root: string, options?: ScanOptions)` with `export interface ScanOptions { ignore?: boolean }` (default true), exported from `src/index.ts` alongside the other scan types. When ignore is not `false`, get the matcher once via `ignoreMatcher(root)`; in the walk, skip a folder (don't descend) when `matcher(path, true)` and skip a file when `matcher(path, false)`, with `path` the existing `/`-joined relative path. Keep existing skips (.git, node_modules, symlinks, binaries). `.locignore` itself is counted like any other file (unless a pattern ignores it). With `ignore: false`, count everything as before. In `src/cli.ts`, accept `--no-ignore` (filter it out of `rest` like `--json` so it isn't 'unknown option') and pass `{ ignore: !noIgnore }` to scanFolder. Write failing tests first in `test/scan.test.ts`: ignored files and folders (with contents) left out, `.locignore` counted, `{ ignore: false }` counts everything, no .locignore unchanged. Optionally test the CLI flag by running the compiled/ts entry only if easy without new deps; otherwise keep the CLI change minimal. `npm run check` must pass.

reviews.summary:
The diff meets the brief. I found no blocker or major defects, and `npm run check` passes. I did not run the code myself; I read `src/ignore.ts` and the diff.

- **`scanFolder` signature:** `scanFolder(root, options = {})` takes `ScanOptions { ignore?: boolean }`, and `ScanOptions` is exported from `src/index.ts`.
- **Matcher:** it is built once, unless `ignore === false`.
- **Walk:** ignored folders are not descended into, and ignored files are skipped before the binary check. The `.git`, `node_modules`, symlink and binary skips are unchanged.
- **`.locignore` itself:** it is counted like any other file.
- **Moved `lstat(root)`:** it now runs before `ignoreMatcher`, so a missing root still fails with the same error.
- **CLI:** `--no-ignore` is filtered out of `rest` and passed on as `{ ignore: !noIgnore }`.
- **Tests:** the new tests cover ignored files and folders with their contents, `.locignore` being counted, `{ ignore: false }`, and no `.locignore`.

nodes.research:
**Findings**

`ignoreMatcher` already exists: `src/ignore.ts` and `test/ignore.test.ts` are on this branch, and `src/index.ts` already exports it. I didn't read `src/ignore.ts`. Its signature should match the brief.

**`src/scan.ts`**
- The signature is `scanFolder(root: string)`. The walk is a nested `walk(dir, rel)` closure.
- `path` is `rel ? `${rel}/${entry.name}` : entry.name`, which is already `/`-joined.
- Order inside the loop: symlink → skip, directory → `.git`/`node_modules` check then recurse, then the file check (`isFile` and `binary`).
- Planned edits:
  - Add `export interface ScanOptions { ignore?: boolean }`.
  - Before the walk, set `const matcher = options.ignore === false ? null : await ignoreMatcher(root)`. Import it with `import { ignoreMatcher } from './ignore.js'`.
  - In the directory branch, add `matcher?.(path, true)` to the skip condition.
  - Add `if (matcher?.(path, false)) continue;` before the `binary()` call, so ignored files are never opened.
- `.locignore` has no extension. `languageOf` will probably return undefined, so it counts as `Text`. Check that when you assert on it in the test.

**`src/index.ts`**
- The scan export line is `export { scanFolder, summarize, type FileCount, ... } from './scan.js'`. Add `type ScanOptions` to it.

**`src/cli.ts`**
- Current code: `const json = args.includes('--json'); const rest = args.filter((a) => a !== '--json');`
- Change it to add `const noIgnore = args.includes('--no-ignore')` and filter both flags out of `rest`.
- Change the call to `scanFolder(folder, { ignore: !noIgnore })`.
- The CLI is top-level ESM with `process.exit`. There is no test for it and no bin entry in `package.json`. Testing it would need `tsc` output or a TS loader, so I'd skip a CLI test as the brief allows.

**`test/scan.test.ts`**
- It has a `folder(files: Record<string,string>)` helper that makes a temp dir, with parent dirs created. Reuse it. The existing import is `import { scanFolder, summarize } from '../src/index.js'`.
- The existing test for `scanFolder` is under `describe('scanFolder')`. Add the new cases there:
  - Ignored files and folders (with their contents) are left out, e.g. `.locignore` = `*.log\nvendor/\n`.
  - `.locignore` itself is in the results.
  - `{ ignore: false }` counts everything.
  - A folder with no `.locignore` gives the same result as before.
- Expected objects have the shape `{ path, language, lines, code, comments, blank }`. Use `.map(f => f.path)` for the simpler assertions.

**Conventions and traps**
- Relative imports end in `.js`. Use `import type` for type-only imports. The existing code is dense, with one-line statements.
- Don't add dependencies.
- Write the failing tests first, then run `npm run check`.
- A `.locignore` pattern like `.locignore` or `*` could ignore the file itself, which is correct.
- Don't skip the `.locignore` read when `ignore:false`. `ignoreMatcher` must not be called at all in that case.
